english.title: Breach of an anti-social behaviour order
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse, did an act, namely **(..SPECIFY ACT..), which you were prohibited from doing by an anti-social behaviour order made under section 1 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 on **(..SPECIFY DATE OF ORDER..) by **(..SPECIFY COURT..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(10) of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
without reasonable excuse did an act
prohibited from doing by anti-social behaviour order

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(I) IMPORTANT - This offence was repealed on the 23 March 2015 - however, by virtue of transitional provisions in section 21 of the Anti-Social Behaviour Crime and Policing Act 2014, any order or interim order that was in existence at the date of repeal, will continue to have effect until 5 years from that date. Therefore this offence still applies to such orders still in existence but is end dated for the 23 March 2020.
(ii) Prosecution may also be brought by the relevant Local Authority.
(iii) For the purposes of this offence, it is not open to the court to make an order under subsection (1)(b) (conditional discharge) of section 1A of the Powers of Criminal Courts Act 1973 in respect of the offence.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
